source_title: Top News Audio Briefing - 27 Oct 2026, 4 AM - The Times of India
source_excerpt: 1- Good evening and welcome to the Times of India's Top News Audio Briefing. We bring you the day's most important headlines from India and around the world. 2- And a warm welcome from me too. We begin today with political developments in India, where the Congress party continues its offensive against the government. 3- Indeed. Rahul Gandhi has urged traders in Delhi to ask Prime Minister Narendra Modi to sack Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. This comes days after concerns were raised about the impact of the 'Chalo Delhi' rally on business. 4- Gandhi posted on X, stating that with a 'stolen vote,' nothing is safe, from shops to savings. He claimed protests against 'vote chori' would stop in 30 seconds if Kumar was removed. Meanwhile, Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge also criticized the government over rising inflation during the festival season. 5- Adding to the political friction, the Centre has reportedly not approved a 'mock Parliament' planned by the Congress at Ashoka Hotel, which was intended to feature a symbolic impeachment of Kumar. Sources suggest it may now be held at Ramlila Maidan. 6- On the other side, the BJP has launched countrywide protests targeting Congress over its president Mallikarjun Kharge's objectionable reference to Prime Minister Modi's father. 7- Union ministers Amit Shah and Rajnath Singh are expected to join this counter-offensive, part of their 'Save democracy, remove anarchy' campaign. Rajnath Singh stated that Kharge's remarks were not just an insult to an individual, but an attack on the dignity of Indian politics. 8- Moving to a significant legal development, the Enforcement Directorate has appealed to the Supreme Court in the NewsClick case, alleging the news portal received nearly 86 crore rupees in 'illicit foreign funding'. 9- The ED claims these funds were received through arrangements designed to make foreign contributions appear as legitimate business transactions, circumventing Indian regulations. They've cited recovered emails and company documents as evidence, questioning the commercial justification for payments from entities like the American Justice and Education Fund. 10- In other Supreme Court news, the court has verbally assured electors that no one will be prosecuted for using Form 6 to re-enter their name in electoral rolls. This allays fears that declaring oneself a fresh voter for re-inclusion could invite prosecution for false declarations. 11- This comes amidst concerns raised by senior advocates about large-scale exclusions from Maharashtra's draft electoral roll, with two crore voters removed, including 1.22 crore due to 'logical discrepancy'. The bench has asked the Election Commission to respond by November 5th. 12- The Supreme Court also agreed to examine whether an MLA or MP who contests a by-election caused by their voluntary resignation should bear the entire expenses incurred by the Election Commission for the previous poll. 13- This development could significantly impact the politics of shifting loyalties. The petitioner has suggested a five-year cooling-off period for such lawmakers, arguing that the public shouldn't pay twice for polls due to an individual's personal or political choice to resign. 14- And staying with legal matters, the Supreme Court will examine the correctness of a Tripura High Court judgment concerning an overage OBC candidate who scored higher than a selected general category candidate but was not chosen for recruitment as a constable. 15- The Centre argues that once an OBC candidate avails age relaxation benefits, they cannot migrate from the reserved category to the general category. The impugned judgment, if upheld, could have far-reaching consequences for recruitment processes across the country. 16- Turning to a tragic incident, five people, four from the same family, were killed and another injured in a shooting at Hotel Bilas Inn in Guwahati on Tuesday evening. 17- Police quickly arrested the alleged killer, Ghanakanta Gogoi, and seized a licensed .32 bore pistol. Preliminary investigations suggest the incident stemmed from a dispute between the hotel owners and Gogoi over a lease agreement. The injured victim is currently receiving treatment. 18- Moving to global business news, Microsoft is extending buyouts to around 60,000 employees across India, the US, the UK, and Canada.
